title: Thirty Seven Days
narrativeQuestion: How did the Sarajevo assassination become a European war in thirty seven days?

chapters.title: Two sides already drawn
chapters.claim: Alliances differed in their obligations; Italy and Britain demonstrate that choices remained.

chapters.title: Small countries, giant empires
chapters.claim: Imperial rivalry and overseas possessions widened the stakes and reach of European war.

namedPeople.name: Bernhard von Bülow
namedPeople.role: Brief source quotation on imperial ambition

chapters.title: A wrong turn on Franz Joseph Street
chapters.claim: The murder of Franz Ferdinand and Sophie triggered a diplomatic crisis, not an automatic world war.

chapters.title: Step through the thirty seven days
chapters.claim: From June 28 to August 4, leaders widened the crisis through backing, ultimatums, mobilization and declarations.

chapters.title: Six weeks to Paris
chapters.claim: The planned rapid victory failed; by the end of 1914 the Western Front had become entrenched.

chapters.claim: MAIN organizes long-term pressures; the assassination was an immediate trigger.

accuracyNotes: Bosnia was occupied/administered by Austria-Hungary from 1878 and annexed in 1908.
Russia backed Serbia without a formal bilateral alliance. The Entente was not a single automatic-war treaty.
Italy remained neutral in 1914. Ottoman entry came in late October/early November.
Map colors indicate political alignment or war involvement, not occupied territory or war against every opponent.
Timeline has ten selected events, not one step for every calendar day. June 28 to August 4 is 37 elapsed days.
Imperial map groups political control; it does not erase Indigenous peoples or imply uniform administration. Area ratios are approximate polygon estimates, not economic or military strength.
